diagnosis.summary: The nightly run for 2026-10-01 (2e2fc3a8) failed quality checks because orders, order_items and payments each arrived at about 40-45% of normal volume. The upstream orders export only contains channel=web: app and marketplace have zero rows, while all hours are present, so this is a filtered export rather than a truncated one. Remediation: request upstream redelivery of orders, order_items and payments for 2026-10-01.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream exported 2026-10-01 filtered to channel=web only. The app (~150/day) and marketplace (~75/day) channels are entirely absent, while web volume (205) is normal. The hour distribution drops evenly with no late-hour cutoff, so this is not truncation. Related order_items and payments dropped by the same proportion. No dbt model changes and no file malformation.

evidence.claim: Run failed in quality_checks on row_count_trend for orders, order_items and payments (40-45% of trailing median); ingest and dbt build succeeded
2026-10-01 orders contain only web channel; app and marketplace have zero rows while web volume is normal
All hour bands are present with a uniform drop, ruling out a truncated/partial export
Landing file is well-formed with contract header and no parse problems; ingest loaded exactly what was delivered
No dbt model changes, ruling out a bad model deploy
Runbook classifies a whole missing category slice across related tables as a filtered export requiring an upstream ticket and redelivery

alternatives_considered: partial_export (truncated file): rejected, all hours present with an even drop and the file ends cleanly with a newline
bad_model_deploy: rejected, no changed models and raw counts are already low before dbt
genuine business drop: rejected, two entire channels going to exactly zero while web stays normal is implausible
rerun_only: would not restore the missing rows because the landing data itself is incomplete
escalate_to_owner(upstream_app_team): redelivery request is the allow-listed action for a one-off delivery problem

proposal.rationale: The upstream export for 2026-10-01 was filtered: raw.orders contains only channel=web (205 rows, in line with web's normal ~200-280), while app (~150/day) and marketplace (~75/day) have zero rows. All hours are present with an even drop, so the file was not truncated. order_items and payments dropped by the same ~55%, so the filter applied across the related tables. The landing file is well-formed and no dbt models changed, so this is a one-off delivery problem. Per the runbook, the fix is to request a full re-export of the three related tables for the day.

applied: upstream re-exported orders (440 rows), order_items (840 rows), payments (417 rows) for 2026-10-01
